cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Stay Until We’re Okay
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until the relationship feels repaired, even if the practical reason for staying disappears.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The kitchen passes inspection. I haven't approved your departure; we still haven't talked about whether we're okay.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stayed to wash up. The dishes are done. Can I go?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The washing-up part is approved. Sit down for the part where you tell me how we got this angry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got ten minutes before the last bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'm allocating nine to us. You may leave in time for your bus, but I don't want 'the dishes are done' to be our last words.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 approves the kitchen but not departure, A3 requires relational discussion after task approval and A5 allocates nine minutes while granting bus departure, making permission the means of retaining presence.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 finished dishes cause A3 explicit separation of work from anger; B4 ten-minute limit causes A5 nine-minute allocation and a stated release time.

relationship.evidence: B2 has completed the agreed work and B4 has a legitimate last-bus deadline, which A accommodates while insisting on discussion.

heightening.evidence: B4 time limit narrows A5 stay to nine minutes; the emotional goal remains rather than being replaced by another chore.

specificity.evidence: A1 unresolved relationship and B2 completed dishes establish both purposes; A5 introduces no contradictory unfinished cup after reread repair.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 allocating minutes like an inspection item gives modest status wit, but the ending is intentionally earnest and somewhat explanatory.
